body.heading: Where in the world is Indonesia?
paragraphs: Indonesia is a country in Southeast Asia, which is part of Asia. It is an island country, surrounded by sea. It is made of thousands of islands — more than 17,000 of them — strung along the equator. It shares a land border with Timor-Leste.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Indonesia is Jakarta. Jakarta is a huge, busy city on the island of Java. A brand-new capital city called Nusantara is being built on the island of Borneo for the future.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Indonesia is Indonesian.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Indonesia is the Indonesian rupiah.

body.heading: How big is Indonesia?
paragraphs: Indonesia covers about 1,905,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about three times the size of Afghanistan.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Komodo dragons are large monitor lizards native to several Indonesian islands. Komodo dragons have a venomous bite and an amazing sense of smell — they can detect a meal kilometres away.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Bali is called the Island of the Gods — families visit sea temples like Tanah Lot, emerald rice terraces at Tegallalang and the art town of Ubud.
In Komodo National Park, rangers lead families to see real-life dragons — Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards — plus pink-sand beaches and manta rays.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Indonesia on a map or globe. Which continent is it nearest to — and what sea or ocean surrounds it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
